title: Question
description: One multiple-choice item. Four options, exactly one correct, every option explained, and at least one verifiable citation.

id.description: Assigned once, never changed, never reused. Attempts reference published snapshots rather than this id, but a changed id would still orphan review history.

course_id.description: The course this question belongs to.

status.description: draft: incomplete work. review_ready: awaiting independent review. needs_review: withdrawn for source drift or a content/evidence concern. published: reviewed and selectable. retired: permanently withdrawn.

objective.description: Cross-checked against the course definition file under content/courses/

stem.description: The question itself. Restricted Markdown, sanitized at build time; executable MDX is not accepted anywhere in this repository.

options.description: Exactly four. Exactly one carries correct: true — enforced by contains/maxContains below. Option text uniqueness is checked by the lint, which JSON Schema cannot express.

explanation.description: Required on every option, including the wrong ones. Explaining why a distractor is wrong is the part that makes this a study tool rather than a quiz.

evidence.description: At least one citation. CI fetches each cited source's private snapshot by hash and asserts the excerpt occurs verbatim; a mismatch blocks publication.

source_sha256.description: Exact immutable SHA-256 hash of the R2 snapshot that supports this claim.

excerpt.description: At most 25 whitespace-separated words, quoted verbatim from the source. The pattern enforces the word cap. If 25 words cannot support the claim, the question is too broad for a single citation — cite twice or narrow the claim; do not paraphrase to fit.

locator.description: Optional human aid for the reviewer, such as a heading or anchor. Never used by the verifier.

by.description: The agent or person that drafted the item. Under CONTENT-POLICY.md the maintainer is not an item author, so a human name here on a content PR is a policy violation, not a formatting problem.

reviewed.description: Approval by a human or independent agent. Agent approvals require a current content fingerprint; legacy human approvals remain compatible.
